rationale: Revise experiment 94c20e41b2ad4cfba9d46911ecede913-experiment to repair a definition defect in its first receipt: comparison 0 asserted add_failed on the result event, but the harness emitted that field only on the case event, so the receipt reports the admission check as unknown (diagnostics: 'Missing required result fields: add_failed' and 'Admitted operation has no complete applicable result observation'). The harness now emits add_failed on the result event as well, which leaves every other input, event field and comparison unchanged and makes the admission assertion evaluable on the same observation the other five comparisons use. Re-executing also yields a second observation of the decisive case: the grown phantom configuration with a reachable new server and a partitioned committed voter. In the first receipt the leader was A and the committed peer B; a local re-run of the revised harness produced the same pair with the roles swapped (leader B, committed peer A: re-elected, commit_index=4, new server at 4, committed peer at 2; control without the new server: no re-election, no commit). The formal run is requested to put that second observation and the repaired admission check on the retained record.

scope.description: Three real nodes over in-memory transports with 300 ms heartbeat, election and lease timeouts. Nodes A and B are bootstrapped with the committed two-voter configuration {A,B}; node C is started with no configuration and no bootstrap, which is the state of a server named by an AddVoter call before that call is logged, and it is reachable from both committed voters. The leader's log store fails exactly the StoreLogs call carrying AddVoter(C), so the in-memory latest configuration becomes {leader, other committed voter, C} at an index the stored log never reaches. The harness then removes the leader's ability to reach the other committed voter in both directions and records whether the leader re-elects, whether a client command commits, and where each of the three logs ends. The trigger leaves C reachable; the control also removes the leader's ability to reach C. The result event reports the failed-write flag alongside the rest of the outcome, so the admission assertion is evaluated on the same observation as the outcome assertions.
assumptions: All three nodes run the captured code; C is a genuine raft.Node with an empty log, an empty stable store and no bootstrap configuration, not a stub that merely answers RPCs.
The injected failure is a single StoreLogs call returning an error; the store accepts later writes.
Cutting a route with the in-memory transport's Disconnect models a network partition, not a process stop: the cut node keeps running and keeps its own view.
A command is treated as committed when its Apply future returns nil, the client-visible completion point.
The committed configuration remains {A,B} throughout, so any commit requires both committed voters, and a commit the other committed voter lacks is unsupported by that configuration.
excluded: No restart, no snapshot and no repair of the phantom configuration after the observation.
No non-voter in the committed configuration and no concurrent client traffic.
The partition is applied after the failed configuration write, so a network failure that precedes or coincides with the write is not exercised.

experiment.prefix: The harness creates three in-memory transports and connects every pair in both directions, bootstraps the two-voter configuration {A,B} on the stores of A and B, and starts three rafts: A and B from their bootstrapped stores, and C with an empty log, an empty stable store and no configuration, so every membership guard that tests a non-empty server list does not apply to it. It waits up to ten seconds for A or B to lead, records which member leads, arms that leader's log store to fail the next StoreLogs call, and calls AddVoter('C', address-of-C) with a five-second timeout. It emits pg_case_<case> with the returned error, the in-memory latest configuration index and servers, the last stored log index and the number of voters in the phantom configuration. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other committed voter's address and that voter's transport from the leader's address, and in the control case also disconnects the leader from C and C from the leader. It waits up to ten seconds for the leader to be Leader again, applies one command with a three-second timeout, and emits pg_result_<case> with the re-election flag, the apply result, the reported failure flag, the leader's commit index, each of the three last log indices, whether the committed voter holds the committed index, whether C holds it, and commit_without_committed_voter, which is true only when the apply succeeded and the other committed voter's log ends below the leader's commit index.
semantic_changes: The result event now repeats the reported failure flag add_failed, which the earlier revision emitted only on the case event; no other event field was added or removed.
The cluster, the injected failure, the partitions, the event names and all six comparisons are unchanged, so the receipt is directly comparable with the first one for this experiment.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns both the durability of a configuration change and the supporter set used for elections and commitment. A configuration entry that was never stored cannot be the configuration under which a node counts votes or commits entries; adopting it anyway lets a server the committed configuration does not include supply the decisive acknowledgement for a commit, so a client is told a command is committed while the committed voters are split.

comparisons.description: The failed configuration write must be reported as a failure in the reachable-new-server case.
The in-memory latest configuration must not refer to an index beyond the stored log after the failed AddVoter.
A command committed while the leader cannot reach the other committed voter must not exist, because the committed two-voter configuration needs that voter.
The other committed voter must hold every committed index, whatever set of acknowledgements the leader counted.
Control: with both the committed voter and the new server cut, the phantom configuration of three voters has no attainable second vote, so the node must not regain leadership.
Control: no command may commit once the only remote voter available to the phantom configuration is also unreachable, which is what shows the trigger's commit depended on that server.

experiment.revision_reason: The result event now repeats the reported failure flag add_failed, so the admission comparison that previously evaluated as unknown can be decided on the result observation; the cluster, the partition, the event names and all six comparisons are unchanged.
